questions.q: Why does this lesson treat privileged accounts as a different risk category from regular user accounts?
options: A compromised privileged account can touch almost everything in the environment, giving it an outsized blast radius
Privileged accounts are always used by external vendors, never employees
Privileged accounts cannot be protected by any technical control
Regular user accounts are never targeted by attackers
questions.explain: Examples given — database sysadmin, domain administrator, cloud subscription owner — can read any table, change any permission, or disable logging, unlike a regular account scoped to one job's needs.

questions.q: What does a PAM (privileged access management) vault change about how administrators use elevated accounts?
options: The password lives in a vault the admin doesn't directly know; they check it out for a session and it can rotate afterward
It gives every administrator a permanent, unchanging password for convenience
It removes the need for any administrative accounts at all
It requires administrators to share one single password forever
questions.explain: This closes problems like shared admin passwords, passwords that never rotate, and having no record of who used a shared account on a given day.

questions.q: How does just-in-time elevation apply specifically to admin rights, per this lesson?
options: An administrator requests elevation for a bounded window and it's automatically removed when that window closes
Administrators hold sysadmin rights permanently from their first day
Elevation is granted once and never reviewed again
JIT elevation only applies to read-only permissions, never admin rights
questions.explain: The account spends most of its time at normal-user privilege and is only briefly, deliberately elevated when there's an actual task requiring it.

options: A last-resort privileged credential used only when the normal privileged-access system itself is unavailable
The primary account every administrator uses for daily tasks
A type of encryption key used for data at rest
An account automatically created for every new hire
questions.explain: Break-glass accounts exist for the scenario where the PAM vault or identity provider itself is down; they're used rarely, and every use triggers an alert and mandatory review.

questions.q: What is the purpose of session recording for privileged accounts?
options: To log the commands and screens of a privileged session so there's a precise record if something goes wrong
To automatically block all administrative commands from running
To replace the need for a PAM vault entirely
To encrypt the database at rest during the session
questions.explain: Session recording provides an after-the-fact record of a privileged session's activity, rather than relying on memory or checkout logs alone.
